title: Krishan Pathak Returns as India Name Squad for Home Asian Champions Trophy in Punjab
excerpt: Harmanpreet Singh captains an 18-member squad for the October 27–November 5 tournament in Jalandhar and Mohali. Defending champions India — five-time winners — keep the core of the Asian Games gold side, with Amandeep Lakra and Aditya Arjun Lalage the young faces retained.
body:
• Hockey India announced an 18-member men's squad on Tuesday for the Asian Champions Trophy Punjab 2026, to be played in Jalandhar and Mohali from October 27 to November 5.
  • Goalkeeper Krishan Bahadur Pathak returns to the squad alongside Suraj Karkera; captain Harmanpreet Singh leads a side that retains the core of the Asian Games gold-medal team.
  • Young defender Amandeep Lakra and midfielder Aditya Arjun Lalage keep their places, with Vishnu Kant Singh and Angad Bir Singh named as the two reserves.
  • India are the defending champions and the tournament's most successful team, with five Asian Champions Trophy titles.

India will defend their Asian Champions Trophy title on home soil in Punjab with a squad built on continuity — and one notable return. Hockey India on Tuesday named the 18-member men's squad for the tournament in Jalandhar and Mohali from October 27 to November 5, with goalkeeper Krishan Bahadur Pathak back in the group alongside Suraj Karkera, IANS reported.

The squad

Captain Harmanpreet Singh leads the side after guiding India to gold at the Asian Games in Japan, where the team defended its continental crown for the first time. The defence features Amit Rohidas, Jugraj Singh, Jarmanpreet Singh, Sanjay and Amandeep Lakra alongside the captain. The midfield is anchored by Nilakanta Sharma, Hardik Singh and Manpreet Singh, and the attack runs through Mandeep Singh, Dilpreet Singh, Sukhjeet Singh, Abhishek, Shilanand Lakra and Rajinder Singh. Midfielder Vishnu Kant Singh and forward Angad Bir Singh are the two reserves.

"Playing the ACT in Punjab will be something special. This squad blends youth with experience, and we can't wait to feed off the home crowd. There's nothing like playing a tournament in India, and we've missed it."

— Craig Fulton, India Chief Coach

Why Punjab, why now

The tournament marks the return of international hockey to Punjab, a state that has produced generations of India's finest players and retains the sport's deepest grassroots culture in the country. League-stage matches will be played at the Olympian Surjit Singh Hockey Stadium in Jalandhar from October 27 to November 2, with the competition also staged in Mohali. India enter as defending champions and the most successful team in the tournament's history with five titles — and, after the Asian Games triumph, as the side every other Asian nation is measuring itself against. For Pathak, whose career has run in the long shadow of P.R. Sreejesh, a home tournament is the stage to make the No. 1 goalkeeper's jersey his own in front of the crowd that understands the position best.
